repl.title: Automatic detection of fast oscillations of dark matter scalar field and updated cosmological constraints on QCDM
repl.summary: It is well known that a scalar field dark matter with a quadratic potential undergoes fast oscillations when the time period represented by the mass scale in the Klein-Gordon equation becomes much smaller than that set by the Hubble parameter. This makes a solution to the equation numerically intractable. Many works in the literature have addressed the problem by either switching between solving the Klein-Gordon equation in the well-behaved regime to solving the fluid equations at the onset of oscillations, or by introducing a new set of variables that can absorb these oscillations. Despite being successful, these techniques rely on an estimate of when the oscillations start. For large scale scans of a model's parameter space, this can become cumbersome. Furthermore, the techniques have been used mainly for non-interacting dark matter models. In this work, we introduce an averaging technique with an automatic detection of the onset of oscillations, capable of capturing the non-interacting as well as the interacting dark matter scenarios. The technique, implemented in \texttt{CLASS}, is tested on the QCDM model and shows excellent detection and averaging abilities. We also update the cosmological constraints on the model using the most recent public data.

repl.title: Hydrogen Engulfment into Sub-Neptune Cores through Magma Ocean Convective Surface Renewal
repl.summary: A convective surface renewal explanation for ingassing of hydrogen from H2-rich envelopes into molten cores of growing planets is presented, with particular application to sub-Neptunes. The ingassing of hydrogen occurs at a moving front comprising the upper boundary of the magma ocean that engulfs hydrogen from the envelope above as it moves. The mechanism of engulfment is surface renewal as the upper diffusive boundary layer is diluted by convection. Surface renewal results in ingassing even where the stabilizing buoyancy of the low-density hydrogen neutralizes the destabilizing thermally-driven buoyancy. It is ultimately driven by cooling. Beginning during the gaseous disk phase, when hydrogen is effectively available in infinite supply, sub-Neptunes can acquire enough hydrogen to permit global core-envelope equilibrium. The structures are therefore consistent with hydrogen-rich, supercritical magma oceans overlain by hydrogen-rich envelopes. The process of surface renewal has implications for other magma ocean - atmosphere interactions in general.

repl.title: Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots Require Free-Fall Growth
repl.summary: Supermassive black holes/active galactic nuclei (SMBHs/AGN), forming only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang as observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), challenge theoretical understanding. How could they grow so massive $(M_{\rm BH} > 10^6 {\rm \,M}_\odot)$ so quickly after initial seeding? Is this rapid growth related to the numerous and enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources with AGN-like characteristics, discovered by JWST? To address these mysteries, we consider the first-order constraint on SMBH growth: enough baryonic material has to reach the vicinity of the SMBH seed, located near the bottom of the gravitational potential well of the host dark matter halo. We specifically examine cold-mode accretion, where gas from the cosmic environment flows into the virialized halo in cold streams without being shock-heated, efficiently reaching the center on a free-fall timescale. We find that cold mode accretion is necessary to supply material for the SMBHs to reach the observed masses, whereas for shock-heated gas inflow the required amount could only be supplied by implausibly rare halos. Moreover, cold-mode inflow in rare $(\sim1$ Gpc$^{-3}$) halos matches the mass and number of the massive quasars, and halos able to support super-Eddington accretion for massive SMBHs ($\sim10^7$ M$_\odot$) match LRD number densities. The decreasing LRD abundance at lower redshifts may then reflect the termination of cold-mode accretion in the growing host halos. The populations of massive SMBHs and LRDs at early times may thus arise naturally from cosmological structure formation, based on the abundance of halos capable of supplying sufficient material through cold accretion.

repl.title: A systematic search for long GRBs without supernovae: global properties and rate of events
repl.summary: Some long duration gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) are not associated with bright supernovae (SNe), indicating that their explosion mechanism differs from the traditional collapsar channel. SN-less LGRBs are rare, thus it remains unclear whether they are sporadic outliers or a substantial component of the GRB population. In this work, we use two decades of Swift observations to conduct a systematic search for nearby ($z\lesssim$0.35) LGRBs without a confirmed SN association. Our analysis reveals a heterogeneous population linked, in part, to star-forming or dusty environments and, in part, to quiescent galaxies. Through the analysis of their high-energy properties, afterglows, and environments, we identify a sample of LGRBs with robust SN limits and distance scales, more than doubling the number of candidate SN-less events. From our fiducial sample, we derive a volumetric rate, not corrected for beaming, of $R = (0.5 \pm 0.2) {\rm~Gpc^{-3}\ yr^{-1}}$, comparable to the apparent rate of short duration GRBs (SGRBs) and standard LGRBs with SNe with luminosities $L \gtrsim\,10^{50}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$. For plausible beaming factors, the inferred rate of SN-less LGRBs is consistent with several compact binary merger channels, although the allowed parameter space is already narrow if the entire population is attributed to a single progenitor channel. Owing to the small number of candidate events and the uncertainties in their distance scale, our sample leaves the low-luminosity tail unconstrained. A larger sample will be needed to determine whether they are the faint tail of known progenitor channels or evidence of a distinct route to relativistic explosions.

repl.title: Kink instability as a particle acceleration mechanism in X-ray binaries and the connection to the outburst cycle
repl.summary: We consider whether the kink instability can explain particle acceleration in hard state 'compact' X-ray binary jets. We apply a 1D model to assess the expected growth rate of the instability for a variety of jet models, then scale results from simulations to estimate a dissipation rate for the magnetic energy in the jet. We then consider the effects of radiative cooling on the system. We find that hard state 'compact' X-ray binary jets are likely to be unstable to the kink instability within their acceleration zones across a plausible parameter space. We further find that depending on the parameters of the model, the jets may radiate over a variety of length scales ranging from length scales attributable to a 'failed' jet scenario, to those in keeping with resolved radio observations of 'compact' jets. We discuss the expected evolution of this model through the outburst cycle.

repl.title: The 1.6 $μ\mathrm{m}$ $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump as a diagnostic of TP-AGB contributions and recent quenching. I. Insights from stellar population models
repl.summary: The 1.6 $\mu\mathrm{m}$ $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump arises from a minimum in the opacity of the negative hydrogen ion in cool stellar atmospheres. Although it is recognized as a common feature in galaxy spectra, its potential for studying stellar populations and recent quenching remains underexplored. Its enhancement at intermediate ages is strong in some stellar population models with substantial thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) contributions but weak or absent in others. This variation makes the feature both a potential age diagnostic and a source of model uncertainty. We use models based on the X-shooter Spectral Library (XSL) and Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis (FSPS) to examine what drives this behavior and what it can reveal about quenching. Controlled FSPS experiments show that the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump depends on both the amount of TP-AGB light and the stellar template used to represent it. The adopted XSL and TP-AGB-on FSPS models predict a transient enhancement of the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump following rapid quenching, while optical spectral features D4000 and H$\delta$ produce monotonic responses. Combining these diagnostics can therefore provide additional information about recent quenching, although the interpretation depends on the population model and star-formation history. The $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump -- $\mathrm{D}4000$ plane shows that models including TP-AGB contributions can describe the observed JWST NIRSpec data reasonably well. These results motivate further use of the $\rm{H^{-}}$ bump to test TP-AGB prescriptions and investigate quenching with current and forthcoming observations.

repl.title: Widespread steep X-ray spectra of luminous $z=5.85-7.64$ quasars and their implications for future X-ray surveys
repl.summary: Luminous quasars (QSOs) at the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, $z\gtrsim6$) host billion-solar-mass black holes assembled within the first Gyr of cosmic time. Their X-ray emission probes the innermost accreting regions and constrains the physical state of the corona during early supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth. Previous results from the HYPerluminous quasars at the Epoch of ReionizatION (HYPERION) sample of $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs, powered by the most rapidly accreted SMBHs, suggested a link between X-ray spectral slope and long-term growth efficiency. We test whether the steep X-ray spectra of luminous z>6 QSOs are a general property of early SMBH growth or a peculiarity of the most efficiently grown SMBHs, using a sample extended mainly to the lowest growth efficiencies. We analysed the largest and most X-ray sensitive sample of 28 luminous QSOs at $z = 5.85-7.64$ (26 used in the correlation analysis), combining HYPERION targets, luminous non-HYPERION sources, and QSOs powered by moderately accreting SMBHs newly observed in our XMM-Newton Large Programme. We re-derived black hole masses and growth indicators for the entire sample homogeneously, incorporating the latest JWST-based spectroscopic measurements to ensure the most consistent and high-quality characterization across all targets. We found no statistically significant correlation between coronal spectral parameters and BH growth indicators: luminous $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs systematically show steep X-ray continua, with high photon indices and/or low high-energy cutoffs, consistent with cold coronae, possibly linked to rapid accretion. Finally, if steep X-ray slopes are common among early AGN, they may significantly reduce count rates, at fixed intrinsic luminosity, in future surveys of the EoR, affecting the detectability of steep-spectrum X-ray sources and thus the census of the early AGN population.

repl.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
repl.summary: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

repl.title: Multi-Method Machine Learning Classification of Astronomical Sources with Rubin Data Previews: a Spectroscopy-Free Approach with DP1 and DP2
repl.summary: We present a multi-method machine-learning study for the binary photometric classification of point-like and extended sources in the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 1 (DP1) and Data Preview 2 (DP2). The workflow runs on the Rubin Science Platform using DP1 and DP2 ugrizy photometry, the DP1 ancillary photometric-redshift catalog, and the Monster astrometric and photometric reference catalog, without relying on external spectroscopy. Six methods (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, k-Nearest Neighbors, an Artificial Neural Network, and a soft Voting ensemble) are benchmarked in the deepest DP1 field, the Extended Chandra Deep Field South. These methods reach 10-fold cross-validation macro-F1 scores of 0.95-0.97 on the balanced training subset and test macro-F1 scores of 0.87-0.92 on the imbalanced held-out set, with RF and the SV ensemble tied at the top (0.918); the differences among the leading methods are within the statistical uncertainty. Permutation importance identifies FWHM as the dominant feature, and the six methods agree on 79.5% of the full catalog. The same pipeline is then applied without retuning the settings to the two other DP1 fields with full ugrizy coverage and photometric-redshift support, Euclid Deep Field South and the Low Galactic Latitude Field. Together, the three fields span a factor of approximately 7 in E(B-V) and approximately 10 in stellar density, yet headline macro-F1 remains above 0.87 in every field. We then apply the same pipeline to four DP2 fields (ECDFS, COSMOS, EDFS, and ELAIS-S1). Using colors and morphology, the best method reaches a test macro-F1 of 0.83 to 0.88 across these fields, and the six methods agree on 77 to 86% of each catalog. Adding the per-band photometric uncertainties as features raises the best macro-F1 to about 0.95 in ECDFS DP1 and 0.97 in ECDFS DP2 (and to approximately 0.97-0.98 in the other fields).

repl.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
repl.summary: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band 6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.

repl.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$α$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
repl.summary: We present H$\alpha$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$\alpha$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$\alpha$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$\alpha$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm H\alpha}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $\alpha_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

repl.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). An overview of the Science Ground Segment architecture and operations
repl.summary: The Euclid mission is designed to address fundamental questions on the nature of dark energy and dark matter by mapping the extragalactic sky with a wide-area survey complemented by targeted deep observations. The required scientific performance places stringent demands on the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), which transforms raw telemetry into calibrated, validated, and scientifically exploitable products. The SGS is a distributed system comprising the Euclid Science Operations Centre, the Science Data Centres, Instrument Operation Teams, and supporting Organisation Units, within a common architectural and procedural framework. This paper presents the SGS as implemented for Data Release 1 (DR1), describing its organisation, architecture, processing functions, and operational model. We outline the main components of the SGS common infrastructure. A key element is the Euclid Archive System (EAS), the central metadata repository based on a common data model. It comprises a Distributed Storage System, providing scalable storage of data files across the Science Data Centres; a Data Processing System used by the pipelines to register and access files and their lineage; and a Science Archive, distributing validated data products. Processing is coordinated by a common orchestration framework based on the Infrastructure Abstraction Layer, providing workflow management and resource abstraction of distributed compute clusters. Software development, integration, and deployment are supported by the Common Development Environment. We describe daily operations, calibration, and quality control, followed by the DR1 production campaign, including processing flows, validation strategy, and computational and data volumes. This infrastructure enabled Euclid DR1, involving 35 million jobs across nine Science Data Centres and 6.7 million core-hours, demonstrating robustness and scalability of the SGS.

repl.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): NISP-P point-spread function modelling pipelines
repl.summary: The images collected in photometric mode by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) instrument of the Euclid satellite are used to model the point-spread function (PSF) of a selection of sources detected in single and combined frames. We used Q1 and DR1 data to improve the development of the PSF module of the near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) and to refine the models currently provided. We explored a few methods normally used to evaluate the quality of the derived models and discuss possible variations related to the position of the sources in the focal plane and to the wavelength and time of the observations. The procedure of fitting the PSF profile, compared to other methods used for flux estimation, such as aperture photometry, indicates that updated models are better than those provided by Q1 images. The current results are in agreement with several key requirements defined for the mission, but there is still room for further improvements, which we plan to investigate and implement in future releases.

repl.title: Orion I: Discovery of an Isolated dE,N Galaxy at 60 Megaparsecs
repl.summary: Inspection of deep JWST images centered on the lensing cluster of galaxies MACS J0454.1-0300 reveals a small, well resolved stellar system that is clearly in the foreground. Photometric measurements including a color-magnitude diagram and radial profile show that it is a nucleated dwarf early-type galaxy (dE,N) at a distance of ~60 Mpc and with structurally normal properties. This object (J04:54:07.39-02:59:22.5, referred to as Orion I for shorthand) may be an outlying member of a previously known small galaxy group, or may be simply an isolated field galaxy depending on the accuracy of its distance estimate. The discovery of Orion I suggests that other small stellar systems in the nearby universe might be found through a search of the many deep \jwst imaging fields that are now being accumulated.

repl.title: Multi-epoch imaging observations of the Galactic Center with NIRCam and MIRI
repl.summary: The center of the Milky Way is the densest and most extreme environment in our Galaxy, its most active star forming region, and the only galaxy nucleus where we can resolve stars down to about a solar mass on the main sequence. The Galactic Center (GC) contains a nuclear stellar disk, a nuclear star cluster, and a supermassive black hole, all embedded within the so-called Central Molecular Zone, which showcases conditions of the interstellar medium that are typically found in high-redshift star-forming regions. The GC hosts the highest concentration of massive stars in the Milky Way and hosts a large concentration of rare objects, such as Wolf Rayet stars and X-ray binaries. The GC is therefore an astrophysical target of outstanding importance. A multi-epoch JWST program enables novel science including the lifetime of planet-forming disks, the search for intermediate mass black holes, direct measurements of the multi-scale gravitational potential, and a deep measurement of the star formation history. Multi-epoch imaging observations with JWST's NIRCam and MIRI instruments will go far beyond Roman WFI surveys in terms of depth and astrometric and photometric precision because of its $3\times$ better resolution, and it expands spectral coverage in narrow bands and mid-infrared wavelength coverage. The proposed observations would correspond to a Treasury Program of about 420\,h, distributed over three epochs spaced three to five years apart.

repl.title: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk$-$new insights from GALAH DR4
repl.summary: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk has drawn extensive attention since ESA's \textit{Gaia} launch. Complex structure appears across a multi-parameter space of stellar abundances, ages, and kinematics. Using GALAH DR4, we investigate ridge and phase-spiral structures in chemical-abundance, phase ($v_i,x_i$), action--angle ($J_i,\theta_i$), and frequency--action ($\Omega_i,J_i$) spaces ($i=R,\phi,z$). Our sample includes 333,412 disk stars with reliable chemodynamical data. In the $R$--$v_\phi$ plane, ridges trace near-constant $J_\phi$ tracks and show coherent variations in $\theta_R$ and $\theta_\phi$. In $J_\phi$--$J_R$, ridges are most prominent when encoded by $z_{\rm max}$ and preferentially associate with metal-rich, low-$\alpha$ populations. In the solar neighbourhood ($R=7.2$--$9.2$\,kpc), we recover a clear phase spiral in $z$--$v_z$. Encoded in $v_\phi$, $\Omega_R$, or $\Omega_\phi$, one-armed spirals appear, whereas the $v_R$-encoded map shows a two-armed spiral. Projecting actions onto $z$--$v_z$ reveals residual spiral signatures in $J_R$ and $J_\phi$, indicating that the phase spiral encodes in-plane orbital information. Both structures depend on age: ridges remain at similar locations with varying contrast, while the phase spiral is more tightly wound in younger and more loosely wound in older populations. Several ridges correspond in $J_\phi$ to known moving groups, and excluding stars in all six moving-group regions makes the phase spiral less distinct in mean radial velocity maps. These links support interpreting ridges, phase spirals, and moving groups within a common phase-space dynamical framework. Combined with trends in orbital properties, age, and abundance, these findings suggest a common dynamical origin and distinct chemodynamical responses of a perturbed Galactic disk.

repl.title: Imprints of screened dark energy on nonlocal quantum correlations
repl.summary: We investigate how screening mechanisms, reconciling light scalar fields driving cosmic acceleration with local fifth force constraints, can be probed via their impact on nonlocal quantum correlations between entangled spin pairs, whose evolution on a curved background is affected by General Relativity (GR) and screened modified gravity effects. We consider a gedankenexperiment featuring a pair of massive, spin-$1/2$ particles orbiting the Earth, evaluating their nonlocal correlations through spin observables associated to the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. Using a general formalism developed earlier for curved space-time spin evolution, we compute the effects of screening on the CHSH inequality, finding its degree of violation to be suppressed relative to the flat space-time case. Applying this formalism to the chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton mechanisms, we identify currently unconstrained regions of parameter space where the screening contribution is comparable to that of GR. While detecting these effects will be challenging, our work provides a proof-of-principle for testing screened dark energy through quantum nonlocality.

repl.title: Probing Dark Matter Interactions with Stellar Motion near Sagittarius A*
repl.summary: Stars orbiting Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) at the Milky Way's center provide a unique laboratory to test gravity and dark matter (DM). We demonstrate that DM interactions in stellar interiors induce a novel momentum transfer force, altering orbits beyond gravitational effects. We derive the first astrophysical constraints on DM-nucleon scattering using S2's 2000-2019 orbital data probing sub-GeV parameter space for specified DM distributions near Sgr A*. We further show that complementary orbital survival constraints and future observations of highly eccentric S-stars extend the reach to DM profiles allowed by present gravitational measurements. Unlike bounds requiring DM capture and annihilation, our constraints apply broadly to scattering DM including asymmetric DM, and extend to masses where methods based on capture can lose sensitivity. Stellar lifetime constraints over Myr timescales complement these, surpassing some direct detection and cosmological limits. This work establishes stellar dynamics as a novel probe of DM interactions.

The red region denotes where DM scattering effects on S2 in 2000-2019 data cause deviations exceeding measurement uncertainties [ 17 ] . Dashed lines correspond to deviations of 10 km s -1 in RV or 100 μ \mu as in RA or Dec over 20 yr period, comparable to current and near future sensitivities [ 17 , 3 , 41 , 27 , 36 ] . repl.title: Bounds on screened dark energy from near-Earth space-based measurements
repl.summary: We test screened dark energy with near-Earth, space-based measurements. In a post-Newtonian framework, we compute leading corrections to geodetic precession (Gravity Probe B), LAGEOS-2 pericenter advance, and the Sagnac delay in a prospective orbital configuration, yielding bounds on chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton models. LAGEOS-2 sets the strongest Earth-orbit limits on symmetron and dilaton, while a Sagnac setup at the projected sensitivity of state-of-the-art space clocks gives the tightest chameleon constraint. These results show that low-density, space-based experiments sensitively probe screened dark energy and exclude previously allowed parameter space. Notably, at an assumed delay precision of $\mathcal{O}\big(10^{-19}\big)$, a Sagnac test would exclude the entire chameleon parameter space considered.

repl.title: Nonlocal Corrections to Scalar Field Effective Action in de Sitter spacetime
repl.summary: We investigate the one-loop effective action for a test scalar field in a general Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) background, specifically focusing on quantum corrections up to the second order in the interaction strength. By employing the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we derive the equation of motion for the field expectation value, which incorporates not only the standard local radiative corrections but also novel nonlocal features: a memory term and a stochastic noise term. We identify all ultraviolet divergent structures within these nonlocal terms and provide a consistent renormalization procedure. To analyze the physical impact of these terms, we apply a local approximation under the assumption of slowly-varying fields, by which the memory term acts as a negative contribution to the drift coefficient. As a concrete application, we consider a massive $\phi^4$ theory and show that these one-loop corrections lead to a suppression of the field variance in the infrared regime compared to the tree-level results.

repl.title: Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
repl.summary: Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

repl.title: Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto-neutron stars
repl.summary: We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp this http URL surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the RMF models with smaller symmetry energy slopes result in various pasta phases at low temperatures, whereas those with larger symmetry energy slopes yield only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust and play an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.

repl.title: The Majoron Cosmological Window: Dark Matter and Thermal Leptogenesis
repl.summary: The majoron is the Nambu-Goldstone boson associated with the spontaneous breaking of a global $B-L$ symmetry. Remarkably, the minimal majoron framework can simultaneously address three key empirical indications of physics beyond the Standard Model: neutrino masses, the matter-antimatter asymmetry, and dark matter. In this work, we identify the cosmologically viable region in which majoron dark matter and high-scale thermal leptogenesis can be realised simultaneously. We show that successful leptogenesis plays a central role in making this scenario predictive: by constraining the right-handed-neutrino mass scale, it determines the irreducible freeze-in contribution to the majoron abundance and fixes the size of the couplings relevant for visible dark matter decays. Combining the irreducible dark matter production mechanisms with warm dark matter limits and indirect searches for decaying dark matter, we map the resulting majoron cosmological window and show that future X- and gamma-ray telescopes can probe part of the surviving parameter space.

repl.title: Dynamical tidal response of neutron stars: From effective field theory to gravitational waveforms
repl.summary: We investigate the fully relativistic dynamical tidal response of neutron stars up to second order in the frequency. Combining the worldline effective field theory for extended gravitating bodies with perturbation theory of relativistic stellar models, we derive the tidal deformation induced by an external time-dependent field, including a universal logarithmic running term. In the effective theory, we work in dimensional regularization and, through a consistent matching procedure, obtain for the first time the complete leading-order dynamical tidal corrections to both the conservative dynamics and the gravitational-wave signal of compact binaries, including the scheme-dependent finite terms in addition to the running. We show that, in the relativistic regime, dynamical effects cannot be fully captured by mode excitations alone. The magnitude of the additional contribution depends on the stellar compactness, the equation of state, and the running term. Dynamical Love numbers are significantly enhanced with respect to their static counterparts for relatively small compactness. As a result, although they formally enter the gravitational-wave phase at eighth post-Newtonian order, dynamical tidal effects yield a nonnegligible contribution during the late inspiral. Using a Fisher-matrix analysis, we show that third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope could measure dynamical Love numbers for a range of neutron-star masses and equations of state. Conversely, neglecting these effects can lead to significant biases in the inference of static Love numbers, and hence on the nuclear equation of state. Our results highlight the importance of dynamical tidal effects for high-precision gravitational-wave modeling with future detectors.

repl.title: Parameter Estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a Binary Merger Triggers with Sub-solar Mass Components
repl.summary: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

repl.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
repl.summary: Detecting maneuvers of non-cooperative satellites is essential for space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid the tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, the statistics already depend on the TPM through the interaction step, and the dependence forms a feedback loop. The loop itself can raise the maneuver probability in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is decoupled from the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geostationary target. In the simulation, the reference filter keeps its sensitivity after small maneuvers, whereas the NIS of the coast sub-filter of the IMM is reduced by the interaction step. RD-IMM detects 1-3 m/s maneuvers, which the fixed-TPM IMM rarely detects, with a false-declaration rate below the false-alarm probability of 0.05 set for the reference filter. In the first hour after the 1-3 m/s maneuvers, RD-IMM also has a lower position error than the compared filters.

repl.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
repl.summary: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.
